newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian candidate concussed, rival stoned.
newsitem.headline: Croatian candidate concussed, rival stoned.

text.p: Vlado Gotovac, one of two challengers to President Franjo Tudjman in Croatia's presidential election next week, is suffering from concussion after being struck on the head at a rally, officials said on Friday.

"Gotovac suffered concussion and bruised soft tissue on the head," Dr Josip Paladino told Reuters. "His situation is stable and we do not expect any complications. He will remain in the hospital under observation for the next 24 hours."

Gotovac, 66, head of the Social Liberal party (HSLS), was flown to a Zagreb hospital after being hit on the head with a belt buckle by a Croatian soldier during an election rally in the Istrian town of Pula late on Thursday.
He looked pale and depressed when he left the plane with a large bandage around his head and he declined to talk to reporters.
The other opposition candidate, Social Democrat Zdravko Tomac, also came under attack but avoided injury.

A stone was thrown at his campaign van in northern Croatia, breaking the windscreen and slightly injuring the driver. Tomac was in a car following the van, the head of his election team, Gordana Sobol, said.
Tomac's van was also stoned in the town of Sibenik last week on its first campaign stop.
The government issued a decree on Thursday saying that all presidential candidates must be afforded full security during the campaign.
But Sobol told Reuters by telephone: that it was unacceptable for the government to decide half way through the campaign that the candidates needed protection.
While both opposition candidates have campaigned unprotected and exposed to provocation by thugs in small towns, Tudjman is guarded by scores of police and soldiers.
The 75-year-old president takes full advantage of his position, using state television as his private media outlet and flying army jets overhead during public rallies.
The Defence Ministry named Gotovac's attacker as army captain Tomislav Brzovic and said he had been suspended from duty and detained, the state news agency HINA reported.
"The Defence Ministry most energetically condemns this violent act," the ministry told HINA, adding that criminal charges were pressed against Brzovic who was drunk at the time.

Brzovic struck Gotovac on the head from behind, his party said in a statement. It said no police reacted until the crowd tried to catch Brzovic who had been pushed from the stage by the party security chief.
Gotovac and Tomac are fighting an uphill battle to try to oust Tudjman, who is expected to win outright with between 60 and 70 percent of the votes in the first round on June 15.

"Standing in these elections is a gesture aimed to show against all the odds that there is another Croatia which resists the present ruling style...and that there are people who are displeased with it," Gotovac told Reuters recently.

Zlatko Tomcic of the Peasant Party, which is backing Gotovac's campaign, said: "Tudjman, his HDZ party and Croatian state television systematically satanise all the opposition leaders, feeding the idea that they are enemies of the state.
"In the uninformed part of the population this falls on fertile ground and awakens base passions," he added.

The HDZ condemned the attack on Gotovac. "We hope Mr Gotovac will continue his campaign without problems," said the head of Tudjman's campaign team. "Unfortunately, such incidents cannot be ruled out but we hope they will not be repeated."
